'''Mickaël Marvin Soriano Piétrus''' ({{IPA|fr|mikaɛl pietʁys}}; born 7 February 1982) is a French former professional [[basketball]] player. Listed at {{Height|ft=6|in=6|abbr=yes}}, {{Convert|215|lb|kg|abbr=unit}}, he played both the [[small forward]] and [[shooting guard]] positions. Piétrus was drafted by the [[Golden State Warriors]] with the 11th pick of the [[2003 NBA draft]], and is originally from Guadeloupe, a [[Caribbean Sea|Caribbean]] island.

Piétrus is also known by the nicknames MP, Air France, Euro Jordan and Puma.<ref name=PietrusBio>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20100406215115/http://mickael-pietrus.com/?page_id=584&lang=us Mickael-Pietrus Bio Page]}}. mickael-pietrus.com</ref><ref>Hu, Janny. (July 15, 2011) [http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/blogs/warriors/detail?&entry_id=27968 Say good-bye: Mickael Pietrus is signing with the Magic]{{dead link|date=February 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}. Sfgate.com. Retrieved on 2012-04-21.</ref><ref>[http://www.pickinsplinters.com/?p=3463 The Undaunted Task of Mickael Pietrus]. Pickinsplinters.com. Retrieved on April 21, 2012.</ref> He speaks French, English, and [[Antillean Creole French|Antillean Creole]] fluently.<ref name=PietrusBio/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2012-06-05/sports/fl-boston-celtics-news-0606-20120605_1_wade-and-james-mickael-pietrus-heat-coach-erik-spoelstra |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303233609/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2012-06-05/sports/fl-boston-celtics-news-0606-20120605_1_wade-and-james-mickael-pietrus-heat-coach-erik-spoelstra |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |title=Celtics bench helping to contain Wade |editor=Harvey, Fialkov |publisher=Sun Sentinel |date=May 5, 2012}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Pau-Orthez===
With [[Élan Béarnais Pau-Orthez|ÉB Pau-Orthez]], Piétrus won the [[LNB Pro A|French League]] championship, in 2001 and 2003, as well as the [[French Basketball Cup|French National Cup]], in 2002 and 2003.

===Golden State Warriors===
[[File:Pietrus 1.jpg|thumb|upright|Piétrus with the Warriors in 2008]]
After leaving France, Piétrus was drafted by the [[Golden State Warriors]]. He played there for five seasons with the last being the 07–08 season.

===Orlando Magic===
During the 2008 off-season, Piétrus was signed by the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nba&id=3482024 Magic land versatile defender Pietrus]. Sports.espn.go.com (July 10, 2008). Retrieved on 2012-04-21.</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3482043 Pietrus leaves Warriors, signs with Magic]. Sports.espn.go.com (July 10, 2008). Retrieved on 2012-04-21.</ref>

In Piétrus's debut, he scored 20 points against the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. He continued to be a key player for the Orlando Magic, with one of his best games being against the [[Dallas Mavericks]], where he made 5 three-point field goals to lead the Magic into a comeback and their first win in Dallas.

Piétrus helped the Magic throughout the [[2009 NBA Playoffs]] where the team reached its second Finals appearance and was a successful defender against [[LeBron James]]. However, he struggled during the final series against the Los Angeles Lakers, as [[Kobe Bryant]] proved too much for him to handle as Orlando fell short in five games.

===Phoenix Suns===
On December 18, 2010, Piétrus was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] along with [[Vince Carter]], [[Marcin Gortat]], a 2011 first-round draft pick, and $3 million, for former Magic player [[Hedo Türkoğlu]], [[Jason Richardson]], and [[Earl Clark]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/orlando_trade_101218.html | title=Suns, Magic Complete Six-Player Trade | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=December 18, 2010 | access-date=December 18, 2010}}</ref> On December 9, 2011, the Suns tried to trade Piétrus and $1 Million to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for a conditional second round draft pick. One day later, Toronto decided to suspend the trade because Piétrus had a problem with his right knee and it would take 2–4 weeks for it to heal. Piétrus was waived by the Suns on December 22, 2011.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7381429/phoenix-suns-waive-veteran-swingman-mickael-pietrus Phoenix Suns waive Mickael Pietrus]. Espn.go.com (December 22, 2011). Retrieved on 2012-04-21.</ref>

===Boston Celtics===
Piétrus signed a $1.3 million deal with the [[Boston Celtics]] on December 24, 2011, two days after Phoenix waived him.
 
On March 23, 2012, Piétrus fell on the floor of the Wells Fargo Center, after being blocked on a layup. He was taken off by stretcher and was diagnosed with a grade three concussion, and ruled out until at least the playoffs. He had been averaging 6.8 points, 2.9 rebounds, and 0.7 assists per game, with the Celtics. He returned in a game against the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on April 11, 2012.

===Toronto Raptors===
On November 30, 2012, Piétrus signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/raptors-sign-free-agent-forward-mickael-pietrus/ |title=Raptors Sign Free-Agent Forward Mickael Pietrus |access-date=November 30, 2012 |archive-date=November 30, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121130200907/http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/raptors-sign-free-agent-forward-mickael-pietrus/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> His final NBA game ever was played on March 20, 2013, in a 101–107 loss to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] where he recorded 2 rebounds and 3 fouls.

===Puerto Rico===
On March 4, 2015, Piétrus signed with [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Mets de Guaynabo]] of Puerto Rico.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/154350/mickael-pietrus-signs-in-puerto-rico-with-mets-de-guaynabo.html Mickael Pietrus signs in Puerto Rico with Mets de Guaynabo]</ref> On May 11, 2015, he was replaced in the line-up by [[Cedric Jackson]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/160777/mets-de-guaynabo-sign-cedrick-jackson-to-replace-mickael-pietrus.html Mets de Guaynabo sign Cedrick Jackson to replace Mickael Pietrus]</ref>

===SLUC Nancy Basket===
On November 25, 2015, Piétrus signed with the French club [[SLUC Nancy Basket]].<ref>{{cite news|title=LES FRERES PIETRUS REUNIS !|url=http://www.sluc-basket.fr/les-freres-pietrus-reunis/|access-date=November 25, 2015|work=sluc-basket.fr|date=November 25, 2015|language=fr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160112115104/http://www.sluc-basket.fr/les-freres-pietrus-reunis/|archive-date=January 12, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==National team career==
In September 2005, Piétrus won the bronze medal at the [[EuroBasket 2005]], with the senior [[France national basketball team|French national team]]. He also played at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110529035848/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp/q/Mickael%20PIETRUS/pid/33932/_/players.html Mickael PIETRUS (FRA) participated in 7 FIBA / FIBA Zones events.]</ref>

==Personal life==
Piétrus' older brother, [[Florent Piétrus|Florent]], is also a professional basketball player.
